findings.issue_text: [High/bug] AdminPermissions.java:77 — the removal-cleanup listener is gated on the V1 feature (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)), so when only V2 FGAP is enabled, ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent no longer trigger permission cleanup, leaving orphaned permission resources/policies

[High/bug] AdminPermissions.java:77 — if V1 is enabled while V2 implementation classes are active, the listener calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...) which throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking client deletion entirely

[Medium/bug] ClientPermissionsV2.java:131-200 — canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, managePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled etc. throw UnsupportedOperationException; any caller reachable under the V2 feature (token-exchange path via canExchangeTo, or admin permissions REST resource reading getPermissions(client)) will surface as HTTP 500 instead of a proper 403/empty response, with no guard showing these paths are unreachable under V2

[Medium/test_gap] PermissionClientTest.java — MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE (canMapClientScopeRoles, the 'map-roles-client-scope' scope) is added to the schema and implemented in ClientPermissionsV2 but has no test coverage; only MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE are exercised in testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient

[Medium/performance] ClientPermissionsV2.java:143-165 — getClientsWithPermission runs a full root.evaluatePermission(...) per client resource inside resourceStore.findByType(...), causing O(N) authorization evaluations per client listing request; should batch-filter (evaluate once against the type resource or query granted permissions) instead of evaluating per client

[Low/doc_defect] ClientPermissionEvaluator.java — requireViewClientScopes javadoc says 'Returns true if canViewClientScopes() returns true' but the method is void and throws ForbiddenException (copy-paste error; other require* methods correctly document 'Throws ForbiddenException')

[Low/bug] ClientPermissionsV2.java:265-278 — getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is private and never called (leftover from removed token-exchange support); the static import AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE and imports ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext, AccessToken, EvaluationContext are only used by this dead code

[Low/bug] PermissionClientTest.java (testConfigureOnlyOneClient / testManageOnlyOneClient) — clientResource.getDefaultClientScopes().get(1) assumes the target client has at least two default client scopes; if server configuration changes the default set, the test fails with IndexOutOfBoundsException rather than a meaningful assertion

[Low/data] AdminPermissionsSchema.java:175-184 — resolveClient accepts either a client internal id or clientId and normalizes to internal id, but permissions created with a clientId string before normalization (or with a stale id after client deletion/recreation with same clientId) will silently reference a non-existent resource name; no migration/invalidation for permissions pointing at resources whose backing client no longer matches

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] AdminPermissions.java:77 — if V1 is enabled while V2 implementation classes are active, the listener calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...) which throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking client deletion entirely

adjudication.rationale: The listener in AdminPermissions.registerListener still handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). The diff adds MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() to return ClientPermissionsV2, where setPermissionsEnabled(...) is overridden to always throw UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). Therefore, if the listener runs in a context where management(...) returns MgmtPermissionsV2 (i.e., V2 permissions implementation is active), a client removal event will trigger an exception, which can break client deletion/cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] ClientPermissionsV2.java:131-200 — canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, managePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled etc. throw UnsupportedOperationException; any caller reachable under the V2 feature (token-exchange path via canExchangeTo, or admin permissions REST resource reading getPermissions(client)) will surface as HTTP 500 instead of a proper 403/empty response, with no guard showing these paths are unreachable under V2

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` is overridden to return a `ClientPermissionsV2` instance, meaning this implementation is now the V2 clients permission evaluator when V2 is used. `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides multiple public methods (`canExchangeTo`, various `*Permission(...)` methods, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`) to unconditionally throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. The diff does not show any guards at the call sites, nor does it demonstrate that these methods are unreachable under V2; therefore the concrete claim about HTTP 500s on specific paths cannot be verified from the diff alone. Still, introducing an active V2 implementation with many unimplemented methods that throw at runtime is a specific, diff-grounded completeness/robustness concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] PermissionClientTest.java — MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE (canMapClientScopeRoles, the 'map-roles-client-scope' scope) is added to the schema and implemented in ClientPermissionsV2 but has no test coverage; only MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE are exercised in testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new client scope string `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` ("map-roles-client-scope") to `AdminPermissionsSchema` and includes it in the `CLIENTS` resource type scopes, and implements authorization logic for it in `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel client)` (checks `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)`). However, the updated/added tests in `PermissionClientTest` only exercise `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` in `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` (permission created with `Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE)`), and do not grant or verify behavior tied to `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`. So the finding about missing test coverage for this newly added nontrivial permission scope is supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] ClientPermissionsV2.java:143-165 — getClientsWithPermission runs a full root.evaluatePermission(...) per client resource inside resourceStore.findByType(...), causing O(N) authorization evaluations per client listing request; should batch-filter (evaluate once against the type resource or query granted permissions) instead of evaluating per client

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission, the code iterates all resources of type AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE via resourceStore.findByType(...), and for each resource calls hasGrantedPermission(...), which invokes root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server), server). This is one authorization evaluation per client resource, i.e., O(N) evaluations for N client resources, which is a concrete performance concern introduced by this new implementation rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] ClientPermissionEvaluator.java — requireViewClientScopes javadoc says 'Returns true if canViewClientScopes() returns true' but the method is void and throws ForbiddenException (copy-paste error; other require* methods correctly document 'Throws ForbiddenException')

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionEvaluator.java`, the new Javadoc for `requireViewClientScopes()` says “Returns true if canViewClientScopes() returns true”, but the method signature is `void requireViewClientScopes();` (a require* method pattern that should document throwing `ForbiddenException`, like other `require*` methods in this interface). This is a real, diff-visible documentation/copy-paste issue, not a behavioral defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] PermissionClientTest.java (testConfigureOnlyOneClient / testManageOnlyOneClient) — clientResource.getDefaultClientScopes().get(1) assumes the target client has at least two default client scopes; if server configuration changes the default set, the test fails with IndexOutOfBoundsException rather than a meaningful assertion

adjudication.rationale: In PermissionClientTest, both testManageOnlyOneClient and testConfigureOnlyOneClient directly index into the default client scopes list with `.get(1)` (e.g., `clientResource.getDefaultClientScopes().get(1)`), which will throw IndexOutOfBoundsException if the client has fewer than 2 default scopes. The diff does not establish that the target client is guaranteed to have at least two default client scopes, so the test can fail due to configuration changes rather than meaningful authorization behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] AdminPermissionsSchema.java:175-184 — resolveClient accepts either a client internal id or clientId and normalizes to internal id, but permissions created with a clientId string before normalization (or with a stale id after client deletion/recreation with same clientId) will silently reference a non-existent resource name; no migration/invalidation for permissions pointing at resources whose backing client no longer matches

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, client resources are newly introduced. When creating or resolving a client resource, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource(...)` uses `resolveClient(session, id)` and stores the *internal* client id as the resource name (`return client == null ? null : client.getId();`). That means a permission created with a `clientId` string will be normalized at creation time (not “silently” left pointing to a non-existent name) as long as the client exists. If the client doesn’t exist, `resolveClient` returns `null` and `getOrCreateResource` will have `name == null`, which is not shown to silently create a dangling reference in this diff. The claim about “permissions created with a clientId string before normalization” also doesn’t match the diff because client resource type support is added here, so there is no prior pre-normalization behavior shown.
